title: Per-run GitHub reachability and credentials
objective: Future GitHub access must be controlled per individual Little Mester run, not by a permanently privileged VM or Unix account. Default runs should not reach GitHub and receive no GitHub credentials, especially no SSH agent/key. Ordinary public internet access may remain allowed; controlling GitHub reachability is distinct from controlling authentication. This is backlog capture only; do not implement as part of Stage A or Phase 1 cleanup.

acceptance_criteria.text: GitHub credentials are denied by default per run; general public network access is allowed and is not treated as credential authorization.
A selected run can explicitly opt in to narrowly scoped, short-lived repository credentials that are available only for that run and revoked or terminated when it ends.
Credentials are not persisted in VM filesystems, OpenCode sessions, workspaces, logs, or reusable shared state, and another run sharing the VM cannot reuse them.
Design distinguishes Git-over-SSH, GitHub API or gh credentials, and public network access as separate capabilities.
High-impact operations such as pushing or merging retain owner approval under the eventual autonomy policy.
GitHub network reachability, including unauthenticated GitHub access, is denied by default for each run, independently of ordinary public internet access.
A selected run can separately opt in to bounded GitHub network reachability and to narrowly scoped, short-lived GitHub credentials; both permissions apply only to that run.
